_comment: Hand-checked derived fields for hot-read.jsonl. Read the fixture top to
bottom against lib/derive.mjs; every number below is a decision the
fixture was written to force.
stalls = 2 -- dial-2 (10012 ms, no channel-open) and dial-3 (9340 ms, no
channel-open). dial-1 reached channel-open and finished. dial-4 failed in
74 ms, which is a refusal and not the 10 s channel-open timeout. dial-5
failed at 9600 ms, inside the stall window, but DID reach channel-open --
it failed at the authentication layer, not at the transport, so counting
it would attribute an admission failure to NAT.
refused_dials = 1 -- dial-4 alone; its detail names the refusal. It is
counted separately from a stall precisely so a per-IP quota mistake (a
fifth instance on the VM) cannot be read as a NAT'd fleet.
first_reads = 4 entries. chunk01 has three preceding candidates (peerA and
peerE from lookup-progress, peerF from discovery) and its first GET went
to peerA -- the second GET to peerE is a FALLBACK and is not recorded.
chunk02 has one candidate. chunk03 has none, so known_holders is 0 (the
client read a peer it had from somewhere other than a logged lookup).
chunk04's GET carries no peer and is skipped -- there is no holder to
name. chunk05's rpc is a PUT, not a GET. chunk06's candidate record
carries its whole set in `detail.peers`, which is absorbed: 4 holders, and
the first GET went to peerG.
